title: Why I'm happy to be back in the office
text:
When my company told us in 2020 that we would all work from home, I was delighted. No more crowded trains, no more expensive sandwiches, no more boring small talk in the kitchen. I could work in my pyjamas and take breaks whenever I wanted. For the first few months, it felt like a holiday.

But slowly, things changed. My living room became my office, and I found it harder and harder to switch off. I answered emails at ten o'clock at night and sat at my laptop all weekend. Some days I didn't leave the flat at all. I realised that I wasn't working less – I was working all the time.

I also missed my colleagues much more than I expected. Video calls are fine for meetings, but you can't have a quick chat over coffee or ask someone a question just by turning your head. As a younger employee, I learnt a lot simply by listening to more experienced people around me. At home, I had nobody to learn from.

So when my manager asked who wanted to come back to the office, I was one of the first to say yes. Now I go in four days a week and work from home on Fridays. The train is still crowded, but I enjoy the clear line between work and home. When I leave the office, my working day is over.

I know that working from home is perfect for some people, especially parents with young children or those who live far from the city. I don't think everybody should be forced back to the office. But I'm tired of hearing that it's the best option for everyone. For me, it definitely wasn't.
